skills.name: benchmarking
skills.description: Guide for building, running, and analyzing Nanvix performance benchmarks. Use this when asked about benchmark setup, execution, or interpretation.

skills.name: build
skills.description: Guide for building, formatting, linting, and spell-checking Nanvix with z. Use this when asked to build or validate the repository.

skills.name: ci-cd-pipeline
skills.description: Guide for Nanvix CI and GitHub Actions workflow behavior, including local pipeline execution and matrix coverage. Use this when asked about CI checks, workflow failures, or release flow.

skills.name: coding-standards
skills.description: Detailed Nanvix coding, documentation, and review standards across Rust, C/C++, Python, and Shell. Use this when asked to implement or review code quality conventions.

skills.name: daemon-development
skills.description: Guide for developing and debugging Nanvix daemons, including guest daemons and host linuxd behavior. Use this when asked about daemon architecture or daemon changes.

skills.name: gdb-debugging
skills.description: Guide for debugging Nanvix guests using GDB remote debugging over the microvm machine type. Use this when asked about attaching GDB, setting breakpoints, or stepping through kernel code.

skills.name: kernel-development
skills.description: Guide for modifying and debugging the Nanvix kernel architecture and kernel-call paths. Use this when asked about kernel internals or kernel implementation changes.

skills.name: library-development
skills.description: Guide for creating and modifying Nanvix libraries under src/libs, including guest no_std and host std crates. Use this when asked about library architecture or crate changes.

skills.name: test-development
skills.description: Guide for writing, running, and debugging Nanvix unit, integration, and system tests in Rust and C/C++. Use this when asked about test implementation or failures.

skills.name: test
skills.description: Guide for running Nanvix tests with z. Use this when asked to run unit tests, integration tests, or the full test suite.

skills.name: troubleshooting
skills.description: Guide for diagnosing Nanvix build, runtime, and test failures, including cleanup and debugging workflows. Use this when asked to investigate errors or unstable behavior.

skills.name: user-app-development
skills.description: Guide for developing, building, and running Nanvix user-space applications across supported runtimes and languages. Use this when asked about guest app implementation or execution.

skills.description: Helps users discover and install agent skills when they ask questions like "how do I do X", "find a skill for X", "is there a skill that can...", or express interest in extending capabilities. This skill should be used when the user is looking for functionality that might exist as an installable skill.

1. // Copyright(c) The Maintainers of Nanvix.
2. // Licensed under the MIT License.
3. 
4. //==================================================================================================
5. // Imports
6. //==================================================================================================
7. 
8. use vstd::prelude::*;
9. #[cfg(verus_keep_ghost)]
10. include!("table.spec.rs");
11. #[cfg(verus_keep_ghost)]
12. include!("table.proof.rs");
13. 
14. use super::{
15.     PteWord,
16.     PTE_WORD_SIZE_LOG2,
17. };
18. 
19. //==================================================================================================
20. // Table Entry Trait
21. //==================================================================================================
22. 
23. ///
24. /// # Description
25. ///
26. /// Trait bound for entry types that can be stored in a page table.
27. ///
28. /// The raw representation uses [`PteWord`] — `u32` on x86.
29. ///
30. #[verus_verify]
31. pub trait TableEntry: Copy {
32.     /// Creates from a raw [`PteWord`], returning `None` if the value is invalid.
33.     #[verus_spec(result =>
34.         ensures result == spec_entry_from_raw::<Self>(raw),
35.     )]
36.     fn from_raw(raw: PteWord) -> Option<Self>;
37.     /// Returns the raw [`PteWord`] representation.
38.     #[verus_spec(result =>
39.         ensures result == spec_entry_raw(self),
40.     )]
41.     fn raw(self) -> PteWord;
42. }
43. 
44. //==================================================================================================
45. // Table Index
46. //==================================================================================================
47. 
48. ///
49. /// # Description
50. ///
51. /// A validated index into a page table, guaranteed to be in `[0, PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH)`.
52. ///
53. #[verus_verify]
54. #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
55. pub struct TableIndex(usize);
56. 
57. #[verus_verify]
58. impl TableIndex {
59.     ///
60.     /// # Description
61.     ///
62.     /// Creates a [`TableIndex`] from a raw `usize`, returning `None` if the value is out of
63.     /// bounds.
64.     ///
65.     #[verus_spec(result =>
66.         ensures
67.             match result {
68.                 Some(t) => index < crate::mem::PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH && t@ == index as nat,
69.                 None => index >= crate::mem::PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH,
70.             },
71.     )]
72.     pub const fn new(index: usize) -> Option<Self> {
73.         if index < crate::mem::PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH {
74.             Some(Self(index))
75.         } else {
76.             None
77.         }
78.     }
79. 
80.     ///
81.     /// # Description
82.     ///
83.     /// Returns the underlying index value.
84.     ///
85.     #[verus_spec(result =>
86.         ensures
87.             result as nat == self@,
88.             result < crate::mem::PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH,
89.     )]
90.     pub const fn into_raw(self) -> usize {
91.         proof! { use_type_invariant(self); }
92.         self.0
93.     }
94. }
95. 
96. //==================================================================================================
97. // Virtual Address Index Extraction
98. //==================================================================================================
99. 
100. /// Extracts the PD index (bits 22-31) from a virtual address as a [`TableIndex`].
101. #[verus_spec(result =>
102.     ensures
103.         result@ == spec_pd_index(vaddr),
104.         result@ < crate::mem::PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH,
105. )]
106. pub const fn pd_index(vaddr: usize) -> TableIndex {
107.     proof! { assert(crate::mem::PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH == 1024) by (compute); }
108.     // The mask guarantees the result is always < PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH.
109.     let index: usize = (vaddr >> crate::mem::PGTAB_SHIFT) & (crate::mem::PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH - 1);
110.     proof! {
111.         assert(crate::mem::PGTAB_SHIFT == 22) by (compute);
112.         assert(index < 1024) by (bit_vector)
113.             requires index == (vaddr >> 22usize) & 1023usize;
114.     }
115.     TableIndex(index)
116. }
117. 
118. /// Extracts the PT index (bits 12-21) from a virtual address as a [`TableIndex`].
119. #[verus_spec(result =>
120.     ensures
121.         result@ == spec_pt_index(vaddr),
122.         result@ < crate::mem::PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH,
123. )]
124. pub const fn pt_index(vaddr: usize) -> TableIndex {
125.     proof! { assert(crate::mem::PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH == 1024) by (compute); }
126.     // The mask guarantees the result is always < PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH.
127.     let index: usize = (vaddr >> crate::mem::PAGE_SHIFT) & (crate::mem::PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH - 1);
128.     proof! {
129.         assert(crate::mem::PAGE_SHIFT == 12) by (compute);
130.         assert(index < 1024) by (bit_vector)
131.             requires index == (vaddr >> 12usize) & 1023usize;
132.     }
133.     TableIndex(index)
134. }
135. 
136. //==================================================================================================
137. // Table
138. //==================================================================================================
139. 
140. ///
141. /// # Description
142. ///
143. /// A page-table page containing [`PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH`](crate::mem::PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH) entries.
144. ///
145. /// This type is parameterized over the entry type to enforce that each table level uses only
146. /// its own entry kind (e.g., PD tables only [`PageDirectoryEntry`], PT tables only
147. /// [`PageTableEntry`]).
148. ///
149. /// The table is accessed via a base address that must be valid in the current address space
150. /// (i.e., a mapped virtual address). It does not own the backing memory — the caller is
151. /// responsible for allocation and lifetime management.
152. ///
153. #[verus_verify]
154. #[derive(Debug)]
155. pub struct Table<E: TableEntry> {
156.     /// Base address of the table (must be page-aligned).
157.     base: usize,
158.     /// Phantom marker for the entry type.
159.     _marker: ::core::marker::PhantomData<E>,
160. }
161. 
162. #[verus_verify]
163. impl<E: TableEntry> Table<E> {
164.     ///
165.     /// # Description
166.     ///
167.     /// Creates a table reference from a base address.
168.     ///
169.     /// # Safety
170.     ///
171.     /// `base` must be a valid, page-aligned address with at least one page of readable/writable
172.     /// memory.
173.     ///
174.     #[verus_spec(result =>
175.         ensures result@.addr == base as nat,
176.     )]
177.     pub const unsafe fn from_address(base: usize) -> Self {
178.         Self {
179.             base,
180.             _marker: ::core::marker::PhantomData,
181.         }
182.     }
183. 
184.     ///
185.     /// # Description
186.     ///
187.     /// Reads the entry at `index`.
188.     ///
189.     /// Returns `None` if the raw value is invalid according to `E::from_raw()`.
190.     ///
191.     /// # Safety
192.     ///
193.     /// The memory at `base + index * size_of::<PteWord>()` must be valid for a volatile read.
194.     ///
195.     // Trust boundary (see `verus-ai-logs/.../tcb-allowed.md` and `verus-unsupported.md`):
196.     // materializes a raw `*const PteWord` from the integer base address (`usize as *const`) and
197.     // performs a volatile load — the hardware page-table access. Verus does not support the
198.     // `usize -> *const T` cast, so the body cannot be verified; this mirrors the
199.     // `bump_allocator::alloc` / `frame::instance` int-to-pointer materialization boundaries.
200.     // The `ensures` pins the (trusted) result to the global page-table memory ghost, exactly as
201.     // `frame::instance` pins its result to `phys_view()` — no exec signature change.
202.     #[verus_verify(external_body)]
203.     #[verus_spec(result =>
204.         requires
205.             index@ < crate::mem::PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH,
206.         ensures
207.             result == spec_table_read::<E>(self@.addr, index@),
208.     )]
209.     pub unsafe fn read(&self, index: TableIndex) -> Option<E> {
210.         let offset: usize = index.into_raw() << PTE_WORD_SIZE_LOG2;
211.         let ptr: *const PteWord = (self.base + offset) as *const PteWord;
212.         E::from_raw(::core::ptr::read_volatile(ptr))
213.     }
214. 
215.     ///
216.     /// # Description
217.     ///
218.     /// Writes `entry` at `index`.
219.     ///
220.     /// # Safety
221.     ///
222.     /// The memory at `base + index * size_of::<PteWord>()` must be valid for a volatile write.
223.     ///
224.     // Trust boundary (see `tcb-allowed.md` / `verus-unsupported.md`): materializes a raw
225.     // `*mut PteWord` from the integer base address and performs a volatile store — the hardware
226.     // page-table write. The `usize -> *mut T` cast is unsupported by Verus, so the body cannot be
227.     // verified; same int-to-pointer boundary as `read`.
228.     //
229.     // No contents `ensures`: page-table memory is *mutable* volatile state, but `write` takes
230.     // `&self` and the global ghost `spec_table_word(addr, index)` is a *pure* function (one fixed
231.     // value per slot). Pinning that pure cell to the caller-chosen `entry` in an `external_body`
232.     // (hence *assumed*) postcondition is unsound — two writes of distinct entries to the same slot
233.     // would assume `spec_entry_raw(e1) == spec_entry_raw(e2)`, and with `lemma_entry_roundtrip`
234.     // that derives `e1 == e2`, i.e. `false`. The slot-update transition
235.     // (`self@.entries[index@] == Some(entry)` after the call, with all other slots framed) is a
236.     // genuine `old@ -> @` state change and is therefore *deferred to the proving-phase page-table
237.     // permission token* — exactly the deferral convention used by `identity_map_view()`'s
238.     // `v -> v'` in `identity_map.spec.rs` (a global accessor whose cross-call transition is
239.     // realized later by a ghost token, "not a verification escape"). Only the sound `requires`
240.     // (in-range index, auto from `TableIndex::inv`) is kept here.
241.     #[verus_verify(external_body)]
242.     #[verus_spec(
243.         requires
244.             index@ < crate::mem::PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH,
245.     )]
246.     pub unsafe fn write(&self, index: TableIndex, entry: E) {
247.         let offset: usize = index.into_raw() << PTE_WORD_SIZE_LOG2;
248.         let ptr: *mut PteWord = (self.base + offset) as *mut PteWord;
249.         ::core::ptr::write_volatile(ptr, entry.raw());
250.     }
251. }
252.

1. verus! {
2. 
3. //==================================================================================================
4. // TableIndex — a validated page-table slot number
5. //==================================================================================================
6. 
7. // A `TableIndex` carries exactly one piece of caller-visible information: the validated index
8. // value. Its abstract value is a single `nat` (see `view_design.md`).
9. impl View for TableIndex {
10.     type V = nat;
11. 
12.     // `closed`: callers reference `self@` and the in-range invariant; the mapping to the inner
13.     // `usize` field is hidden. The abstract value is "the validated slot number".
14.     closed spec fn view(&self) -> nat {
15.         self.0 as nat
16.     }
17. }
18. 
19. impl TableIndex {
20.     // The validated-range guarantee every caller depends on: a `TableIndex` is always a legal
21.     // slot. Enforced as a type invariant so the bound holds unconditionally for any value callers
22.     // hold — this is exactly what keeps `read`/`write` (and `gva.rs`'s `checked_mul`) within one
23.     // page, and is established once at each construction site (`new`, `pd_index`, `pt_index`).
24.     #[verifier::type_invariant]
25.     pub open spec fn inv(&self) -> bool {
26.         self@ < crate::mem::PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH
27.     }
28. }
29. 
30. //==================================================================================================
31. // Virtual-address index extraction (pure helpers)
32. //==================================================================================================
33. 
34. // Low `log2(PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH)` bits of `vaddr >> shift`. Mirrors the exec masking
35. // `(vaddr >> shift) & (PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH - 1)` exactly; the mask makes the result `< LEN`.
36. pub open spec fn spec_table_index(vaddr: usize, shift: usize) -> nat {
37.     ((vaddr >> shift) & ((crate::mem::PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH - 1) as usize)) as nat
38. }
39. 
40. // PD index = bits [PGTAB_SHIFT, PGTAB_SHIFT + log2(LEN)) of `vaddr`.
41. pub open spec fn spec_pd_index(vaddr: usize) -> nat {
42.     spec_table_index(vaddr, crate::mem::PGTAB_SHIFT)
43. }
44. 
45. // PT index = bits [PAGE_SHIFT, PAGE_SHIFT + log2(LEN)) of `vaddr`.
46. pub open spec fn spec_pt_index(vaddr: usize) -> nat {
47.     spec_table_index(vaddr, crate::mem::PAGE_SHIFT)
48. }
49. 
50. //==================================================================================================
51. // TableEntry codec (the per-entry round-trip law)
52. //==================================================================================================
53. 
54. // Abstract serialization / decoding of a `TableEntry`. These mirror the exec `raw` / `from_raw`
55. // trait methods. They are deliberately *unbounded* over `E` (no `TableEntry` bound) to avoid a
56. // definitional cycle (`TableEntry`'s method specs reference these, so a bound here would make the
57. // trait depend on a function that depends on the trait).
58. //
59. // `spec_entry_from_raw` returns `None` for a word that is not a valid encoding of `E` — exactly
60. // the `read` failure path callers map to `InvalidArgument` (see `caller_analysis.md`).
61. pub uninterp spec fn spec_entry_raw<E>(e: E) -> PteWord;
62. 
63. pub uninterp spec fn spec_entry_from_raw<E>(w: PteWord) -> Option<E>;
64. 
65. //==================================================================================================
66. // Global ghost model of page-table memory
67. //==================================================================================================
68. 
69. // Page-table memory is volatile, caller-owned storage the `Table<E>` handle does not contain
70. // (the struct holds only `base`). It is modeled here as a *global, parameter-free* ghost
71. // function — the same device used for the physical-frame subsystem (`mm::phys::phys_view()`):
72. // the abstract state is named globally rather than threaded through a permission parameter, so
73. // `read`/`write` keep their exec signatures and do not cascade ghost arguments into out-of-scope
74. // callers (`identity_map::ensure_pt`/`ensure_pte`/`identity_map_page`).
75. //
76. // `spec_table_word(addr, index)` is the raw word currently stored at slot `index` of the
77. // page-table page based at `addr`. Because it is a pure function, a call to `write` only updates
78. // knowledge about the *one* slot named in its `ensures`; every other slot/page is automatically
79. // preserved across the call (the caller-facing frame condition). The cross-call write transition
80. // (and its consistency when the same slot is written twice) is realized in the proving phase by a
81. // ghost token over the page-table pages — exactly the `phys_view()` "transition realized in the
82. // proving phase" placeholder.
83. pub uninterp spec fn spec_table_word(addr: nat, index: nat) -> PteWord;
84. 
85. // The decoded entry currently stored at slot `index` of the page based at `addr`: the value a
86. // `read` returns. This is the `index -> Option<E>` entry map from `view_design.md`, expressed
87. // pointwise over the global word store.
88. pub open spec fn spec_table_read<E>(addr: nat, index: nat) -> Option<E> {
89.     spec_entry_from_raw::<E>(spec_table_word(addr, index))
90. }
91. 
92. //==================================================================================================
93. // Table<E> — a typed, non-owning handle over one page-table page
94. //==================================================================================================
95. 
96. // To callers a `Table<E>` is a typed handle over the page at a physical/identity-mapped base
97. // address (see `view_design.md`): its caller-meaningful identity is *which page* read/write act
98. // on (`addr`), and its observable contents are the per-slot decoded entry map (`entries`). The
99. // contents live in volatile, caller-owned memory the struct does not store, so the view reads
100. // them from the global `spec_table_read` ghost rather than from struct fields.
101. pub struct TableView<E> {
102.     /// Physical/identity-mapped base address this handle denotes.
103.     pub addr: nat,
104.     /// Decoded entry at each valid slot — `entries[i]` is what `read(i)` returns
105.     /// (`None` = the slot holds a word that is not a valid encoding of `E`).
106.     pub entries: Map<nat, Option<E>>,
107. }
108. 
109. impl<E: TableEntry> View for Table<E> {
110.     type V = TableView<E>;
111. 
112.     closed spec fn view(&self) -> TableView<E> {
113.         TableView {
114.             addr: self.base as nat,
115.             entries: Map::new(
116.                 |i: nat| i < crate::mem::PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH,
117.                 |i: nat| spec_table_read::<E>(self.base as nat, i),
118.             ),
119.         }
120.     }
121. }
122. 
123. } // verus!
